newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to deport Danish journalists.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to deport Danish journalists.

text.p: Sri Lanka will deport four Danish journalists who were in Colombo to cover the case of a young Tamil refugee deported from Denmark earlier this month, their lawyer said on Wednesday.
"They are going to be deported tonight on the orders of the secretary (of the) defence ministry," Gowrysangary Thavarasa told Reuters. "No reason has yet been given."
The four journalists were taken from their hotel rooms for questioning late on Saturday by the Crime Detective Bureau (CDB), Danish Consul General P.B. Rasmussen said.
He told Reuters earlier that he was able to contact the four by telephone at a seaside Colombo hotel, where they were being held under police guard.
The four journalists are Ole Hoff-Lund of the Berlingske Tidende newspaper, Morten Jastrup of Information newspaper, Nis Olsen of Politiken and Jens Moeller of Danish TV2.
The Defence Ministry was not available for comment and it was not possible to speak to the journalists.
Police Crime Detective Bureau chief Lionel Goonetileke told Reuters earlier the journalists were detained under emergency regulations to see why they had visited the island.
The journalists arrived in Colombo last week to follow the case of Chitra Rajendran, an 18-year-old Tamil refugee deported on November 2 from Denmark, where she had sought asylum three years ago.
Her deportation caused an outcry among Danish human rights activists and the Tamil community in Denmark.

According to reports in the Sri Lankan press, Rajendran was detained by police in Colombo on suspicion of having links with the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), with whom two of her brothers are full-time activists.
The LTTE has been fighting for a separate Tamil state in the north and east of the island since 1983 in a conflict that has cost 50,000 lives, according to government estimates.
